text: MCP tool schemas list the target graph's own statuses instead of a fixed set
description:
OBSERVED 2026-11-23: update_idea's description advertises human-dependent, ai-proposition and review, and the Stop hook says to park ideas as human-dependent. Felix's life graph (an older project) doesn't define human-dependent, so the call failed with 'Unknown status' (7218baeb correctly rejects undefined statuses; be32e3a6 only added it to NEW projects). The agent fell back to 'unclear' and lost the distinction between a decision and an action.

Proposal: the error (and ideally get_prioritized_ideas/graph_hygiene) names the graph's statuses; the hook text says 'human-dependent if the graph has it, else unclear'; and a one-time offer/migration adds the standard agent statuses (human-dependent, ai-proposition, review) to older graphs, with the human's OK.

Refuted if all graphs already share the same status set.

status.comment: Accepted by Felix ('can we work on them?'). The error already named the graph's statuses ('Unknown status X. Known: …', e8ac8883). New: a built-in status that an older graph lacks (human-dependent, ai-proposition, review, …) joins that graph's meta.json statuses the first time it's used, under the meta lock, with its default color. Typos still fail. So the tool schema and the Stop hook's 'human-dependent' instruction are true for every graph, with no blanket migration of graphs that never use it, and the hook text needs no 'if the graph has it'. Evidence: new test 'a built-in status an older project lacks joins its statuses on first use' in backend server.test.ts; all 48 server tests pass (Node 22, the stack's runtime) and backend tsc is clean.
